To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a simple, robust, scalable and well-defined solution-phase ligand-exchange method to tune the band edge position of colloidal PbS QDs by 2.0 eV.

the band edge positions (i.e., the energy of the conduction and valence band edges) of colloidal quantum dot semiconductor nanocrystals can be controlled over 2 eV through solution phase surface chemistry modification.

the surface chemistry of colloidal semiconductor nanomaterials can be used to control their band edge positions, which is a crucial parameter for their functionality in many applications such as photovoltatics, photoelectrochmical cells and light emitting devices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new synthetic methods for colloidal semiconductor nanomaterials and their applications in optoelectronic devices.
the design of colloidal semiconductor nanomaterials, specifically quantum dots, for use in solar energy conversion.

the development of new methods to tune the band edge positions in PbS colloidal quantum dots (QD) through solution-phase surface chemical modification, and the establishment of clear relationships between QDs' surface chemistry and their band edge positions.
